title.narrative: GGGI:2022-2025:Biodiversitet för ekosystem och samhällens motståndskraft
GGGI:2022-2025:Biodiversity conservation for ecosystem and community resilience

description.narrative: Det övergripande målet för programmet är att stärka integreringen och integrationen av insatser för bevarande av biologisk mångfald in i lokala utvecklingsprogram genom att: - Förbättra den hållbara skogsförvaltningen i utvalda woredas i utvalda zoner i Oromia och sydvästra Etiopien People Regional States. - Att förbättra jämställdheten mellan könen och försörjningen för skogsberoende samhällen, inklusive kvinnor och ungdomar, och - Bygga kapaciteten hos statliga intressenter och lokala samhällsgrupper vid olika nivåer.

The overall objective of the program is to strengthen the mainstreaming and integration of biodiversity conservation interventions into local development programs by: - Enhancing the sustainable forest management in selected woredas in selected zones in Oromia and South West Ethiopia People Regional States. - Improving gender equality and livelihoods of forest dependent communities, including women and youth, and - Building the capacity of Government stakeholders and local community groups at various levels.

1. Overall Assessment
The 2024 implementation of the CSMFL project registered a number of results under the four outcomes. This is a major improvement compared to last year's implementation, which was output-focused.
Heeding the recommendations given by Sida on the 2023 Annual Report, the 2024 Narrative Report has included a section for "Key Milestones and Results Achieved".
2. Key Results by Theme
a) Biodiversity and Land Use Planning: Key biodiversity areas identified and detailed maps been produced for both regional states (Oromia and South West Ethiopia regions); community participation in conservation was strengthened.
b) Capacity Development: The technical capacity of community forest management cooperatives were enhanced through technical support and training (in sustainable forest management practices); likewise the technical and institutional capacity of local government actors was strengthened through technical support and training (in sustainable forest management, solar power irrigation system and Measurement, and Results Verification (MRV)).
c) Restoration: Degraded forests and agro-forests were restored.
d) Gender Mainstreaming: The capacity of government officials and experts on gender mainstreaming in climate actions and sustainable forest management enhanced by putting to practice the Gender Mainstreaming in Sustainable Forest and Land management guideline developed for the project.
e) Livelihood opportunities for women and youth: Village Economic and Saving Association (VESA) groups established and supported to diversify and strengthen livelihoods options for women; women and youth groups empowered economically by practicing home garden- both agriculture and fruit tree production.
f) Synergies and Partnerships: The project leveraged opportunities like the Green Legacy initiative and established agreements with universities for sustainable forest management research.
3. Key Results by Outcome Areas
Several results are reported under the 4 outcome areas. The following will be a quick highlight (not a summary of the systemic changes).
a) Outcome 1- Improved conservation of biodiversity in the forested landscapes:
- A 10-year periodic review of the three UNESCO biosphere reserves (the Kafa Biosphere Reserve, the Shaka Forest Biosphere Reserve, and the Yayu Coffee Forest Biosphere Reserve) carried out assessing progress and evaluating the reserves' ability to support sustainable development. This is a requirement of UNESCO if these sites are to continue as biosphere reserves.
- Integrated Land-use Plan (ILUP) capacity strengthened: Training on best-practices of ILUP given to zonal and woreda-levels (391 participants (55 female)) and kebele-levels (368 participants (123 female)); 12 Woreda IULP committees formed consisting of 119 members (10 female).
- GIS-assisted land use classification in five project woredas of the Southwestern Ethiopian Peoples Region initiated.
b) Outcome 2- Improved management of forest resources for multiple functions:
- Awareness on Participatory Forest management (PFM) enhanced- a total of 686 participants trained (including 170 females) at the woredalevel involving various social segments at the community level.
- About 8 026 hectares of natural forest demarcated for the PFM scheme across eight woredas; eight GIS-based maps created for PFM forests.
- Since the project's inception, a cumulative total of about 10 079 hectares demarcated for the PFM scheme across nine woredas and fourteen kebeles.
- A total of 1,468 individuals (303 females) registered as PFM cooperative members by paying a registration fee and purchasing shares; community forest management bylaws prepared and approved.
- PFM cooperatives received the forests from the relevant forestry governing body after preparing PFM plan and finalizing PFM cooperative registration.
- To improve the livelihoods of forest-dependent communities, 247 improved modern beehives and accessories were distributed to 477 beneficiaries (230 female); 84% of beehives hold bee colonies, and honey production is expected by mid-December 2024.
- 10 functional tree seed collection groups organized and granted legal recognition by the designated woreda authority to operate forest-related businesses.
- 142 forest-dependent households (70 female-headed households) supported in spice production within their home gardens across 12 project kebeles including ginger, turmeric, and other spices.
- 12 nurseries established and strengthened, creating job opportunities for 104 beneficiaries, including 40 females; these nurseries raised about 344 000 various tree, shrub, and coffee seedlings, generating an income of about ETB 1.1 million.
- Assisted Natural Regeneration (ANR) implemented on 156 hectares of degraded land, which was restored with various plant species and closed off from human and animal interference.
- 66 hectares of degraded land were restored through afforestation and reforestation (A/R).
- 206 hectares of degraded agro-forestry landscapes were restored across various project woredas with a variety of tree and shrub species, as well as improved coffee and fruit varieties engaging 597 households; 182 household parcels were geo-referenced to monitor future changes.
c) Outcome 3: Improved gender equality and livelihoods of the communities in and around the forested landscapes:
- ToT training on gender mainstreaming and climate action was conducted in Jima town, engaging 46 participants (27 women) from government and implementing partners; as a result stakeholders developed gender action plans which fostered a gender-equal environment, and actively engaged sectoral managers and higher officials in gender integration.
- The performance indicators of the Women, Child, Youth, and Social Affairs in promoting gender equality and equity within both the workplace and the community was enhanced.
- VESA Groups: In the Oromia and SWE regions, 75 VESA groups each are established in 2024.
- Technical support was provided to woreda-level government offices on gender analysis, gender-responsive planning, and implementation to enhance their capacity and effectiveness in integrating gender considerations.
- A gender mainstreaming booklet was developed to provide practical recommendations for implementing partners and stakeholders engaged in the project.
- Diversifying livelihood options for women and youth: Through home garden agroforestry and production of high-value fruits, vegetables, tree nurseries, and spices, about Birr 956 000 generated benefiting 552 individuals, including 288 women in the Oromia region.
- A revolving fund scheme was operationalized to provide women with access to sustainable financial services; as part of a pilot revolving fund, six VESA groups with 152 members (145 female) were selected, and Birr 128,000 was allocated to these groups; the VESA groups were equipped with essential tools including functioning management committees and kits(saving box, ledger, passbook, calculator), and bylaws.
- In Oromia, 84 clients (33 females) received training on Vermicomposting production, and 93 households (45 female) received 285 kg of Vermi worms, sourced from early adopters, who sold the worms to diversify their livelihoods;17 farmers (4 women) expanded Vermi composting. In the SWE region, awareness training on Vermicomposting techniques offered to 232 individuals (103 females); as a result, 91 clients (12 females) actively implementing Vermicomposting covering 4.45 hectares of land.
- Capacity development training on solar home systems was conducted for 56 participants (49 men and 7 women) from universities and regional, zonal, and woreda government offices.
d) Outcome 4: Strengthened institutional, human and system capacity and multi-stakeholder coordination
- A multi-sectoral and multi-stakeholder coordination and planning implementation taskforce was established at the project woreda level.
- The project signed MOUs with two universities to collaborate and enhance their capacity in sustainable forest management, fostering technical capacity building and research engagement.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
